_comment: THE DROPPING HALF IS THE HEAD, and it has to be that one rather than the foot (#357).
A two-block block drops from exactly one of its halves or a break pays twice. Which half is not
arbitrary, because MattressBlock.playerWillDestroy removes the HEAD first when the breaker is
creative. Removing it sends a neighbour update to the foot, the foot's updateShape sees its
partner gone and returns AIR, and updateOrDestroy rolls the foot's table on the way out.
So with the condition on `foot`, a creative break of the foot dropped a mattress the player then
kept as well - duplication, and silent, because the survival case still paid exactly one and
looked correct. Vanilla's beds condition on `head` for this reason; ours said `foot` and the
javadoc on playerWillDestroy described the vanilla arrangement the whole time.
